feed.subtitle: AI regulation and critical AI headlines. No cookies, no tracking, no pies.

entry.title: White House finalises a voluntary frontier-model review framework
entry.summary: The administration says it met the deadline for a pre-release evaluation framework for advanced models, but details remain sparse. The key signal is that pre-launch government access has moved from concept toward process. (Source: Axios. As of 2026-08-06.)

entry.title: US policymakers weigh a duty-of-care approach for frontier AI
entry.summary: Senate discussions suggest a framework based on developer self-testing and clearer responsibility for frontier risk, adding legislative pressure beyond executive-order mechanisms. (Source: Platformer AI & Tech Brief. As of 2026-08-06.)

entry.title: California transparency duties become an operative compliance milestone
entry.summary: The amended AI Transparency Act now points providers toward detection tools, manifest-style disclosure, and latent disclosure features where technically feasible, strengthening the synthetic-content governance baseline. (Source: Vorp AI policy tracker. As of 2026-08-06.)

entry.title: EU transparency rules and enforcement powers live from 2 August
entry.summary: Article 50 disclosure duties for chatbots, deepfake labelling, and synthetic-content marking are active, while the AI Office and national authorities begin enforcement. This is the practical shift from planning to operating controls. (Source: European Commission. As of 2026-08-06.)

entry.title: Brussels pairs AI Act enforcement with cyber-focused frontier evaluation plans
entry.summary: Recent EU policy work includes structured access ideas for advanced AI capabilities in cybersecurity and a secure testing platform, showing a tighter link between regulation and operational security. (Source: CDT Europe. As of 2026-08-06.)
